name: Burgio 1998
aliases: Behavioral vs Drug Treatment for Urge Urinary Incontinence in Older Women
question: In older women with urge or mixed incontinence, does biofeedback-assisted behavioral training reduce incontinent episodes more than oxybutynin or placebo?

design.blinding: Drug and placebo double-blind; behavioral arm open to patients and nurse practitioners; diary scorer blinded

arms.label: Biofeedback-assisted behavioral training (4 visits over 8 weeks)
individually titrated oxybutynin chloride (2.5 to 15 mg daily)
identical-appearing placebo capsules with the same clinic visits

design.population: Community-dwelling volunteer women aged 55 to 92 years with urge or urge-predominant mixed incontinence, urodynamic bladder dysfunction and no dementia, screened at a university geriatric clinic.
design.description: Randomized, placebo-controlled, three-arm trial at a university geriatrics clinic
design.locator: PDF pp1-3 (abstract, Methods, Figure 2; journal pp1995-1997)

verdictNote: Behavioral training beat oxybutynin (P = .04) at 8 weeks; durability and long-term adherence were not studied.
takeaway: In 197 older women with urge or mixed incontinence, 8 weeks of biofeedback-assisted behavioral training reduced diary incontinence episodes by a mean 80.7%, versus 68.5% with titrated oxybutynin and 39.4% with placebo; behavioral training beat oxybutynin (P = .04), and both beat placebo.

reports.label: Initial report
reports.citation: Burgio KL, Locher JL, Goode PS, et al. "Behavioral vs Drug Treatment for Urge Urinary Incontinence in Older Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *JAMA.* 1998;280(23):1995-2000. doi:10.1001/jama.280.23.1995
reports.followUp: 8-week treatment period; outcome from the 2-week posttreatment bladder diary

results.measure: Mean percent reduction in weekly incontinent episodes on bladder diary after 8 weeks (behavioral minus oxybutynin shown as the effect; analyzed n = 63, 65, 62)
results.note: SD of the percent reduction 24.8, 37.2 and 80.0. Oxybutynin versus placebo P = .009; behavioral versus placebo P < .001. Pairwise tests were Duncan multiple range tests after a rank-based ANOVA (overall P < .001), alpha .05; the report states no margin or prespecified hypothesis. The 12.2-point difference is subtracted from the reported means.
results.locator: PDF p4, Table 4 (journal p1998); PDF p4 text

results.measure: Mean weekly incontinent episodes after treatment (baseline 15.8, 15.9 and 15.4; P = .98)
Reduction of at least 50% in incontinent episodes
results.locator: PDF p4, Figure 3 and text (journal p1998)

results.measure: Reduction of at least 75% in incontinent episodes
results.locator: PDF p4, Figure 3 and text (journal p1998)
PDF p4, Figure 3 and text (journal p1998)

results.measure: More incontinent episodes after treatment than before
Patients describing themselves as much better
results.note: Table 5 states P < .001 for all comparisons listed in it.

results.measure: Comfortable enough with treatment to continue indefinitely
Wished to receive another form of treatment
results.note: Among subjects not completely dry, 14.5% of the behavioral group wished to add drug treatment and 53.3% of the drug group wished to add behavioral treatment.
results.locator: PDF p5, Table 5; PDF p4 text (journal pp1998-1999)

results.measure: Mean change in cystometric capacity, mL (posttreatment cystometry in 105 of 197 subjects)
results.note: P = .30 behavioral, P < .001 oxybutynin, P = .61 placebo, each versus own baseline.

harms.label: Dry mouth
harms.note: Percent of subjects on the adverse-effects checklist (n = 63, 65, 62); P < .001 across groups.

harms.label: Withdrawal for adverse effects
harms.locator: PDF p3, Figure 2 legend; PDF p5 text (journal pp1997, 1999)
harms.note: None is listed for the behavioral group. Attrition from all causes was 6.2%, 17.9% and 18.5%.

delivery.label: Screening and enrollment
delivery.value: 468 women evaluated; 271 ineligible or did not participate; 197 randomized between July 1, 1989 and August 30, 1995
delivery.locator: PDF pp2-3, Methods, Table 1, Figure 2 (journal pp1996-1997)

delivery.label: Main eligibility
delivery.value: Age 55 years or older; at least 2 urge accidents a week for 3 months or more with urge exceeding stress accidents; detrusor instability or maximal cystometric capacity of 350 mL or less on urodynamics
delivery.note: Excluded: continual leakage, postvoid residual above 200 mL, uterine prolapse past the introitus, narrow-angle glaucoma, unstable angina, decompensated heart failure, malignant arrhythmia, Mini-Mental State Examination score below 20.

delivery.label: Randomization
delivery.value: Stratified by incontinence type (urge only or mixed) and severity (under 5, 5 to 10, over 10 episodes a week); computer-generated random numbers, block size 6

delivery.label: Mixed stress and urge incontinence at baseline
Baseline age and severity (total sample)
delivery.value: Mean age 67.7 years (SD 7.5); 52.8% with more than 10 accidents a week; 48.7% urge only and 51.3% mixed incontinence
delivery.note: The behavioral group had more children, fewer high school graduates (84.4% versus 97.0% and 93.8%) and more rectocele (55.6% versus 32.8% and 54.0%).

delivery.label: Visit schedule and clinician
delivery.value: 4 clinic visits at 2-week intervals over 8 weeks, run by nurse practitioners; daily bladder diary throughout

delivery.label: Behavioral training content
delivery.value: Anorectal biofeedback to teach selective pelvic muscle contraction (visit 1); urge strategies of pausing, sitting, relaxing and repeated pelvic muscle contraction before walking to the toilet (visit 2); repeat or combined bladder-sphincter biofeedback if under 50% reduction (visit 3); review (visit 4)
delivery.note: Home practice: 45 pelvic muscle exercises daily (15 exercises three times), holds built up to 10 seconds; a voluntary stream interruption once a day.

delivery.label: Biofeedback sessions received
delivery.note: No patient received more than 2 biofeedback sessions.
delivery.value: Behavioral arm: 48/65 (73.8%) one anorectal session; 6/65 (9.2%) a second anorectal session; 11/65 (16.9%) a second session with combined bladder-sphincter biofeedback

delivery.label: Oxybutynin dosing
delivery.value: Started at 2.5 mg three times daily, titrated at visits within 2.5 mg daily to 5.0 mg three times daily; final doses 2.5 mg (7.5%), 5.0 mg (19.4%), 7.5 mg (24.4%), 10.0 mg (17.9%), 15.0 mg (26.9%)
delivery.locator: PDF pp2-3, Drug Treatment and Control Condition; PDF p3, Features of Intervention (journal p1997)
delivery.note: Oxybutynin and placebo were dispensed in identical capsules containing 500 mg riboflavin phosphate as a marker.

delivery.label: Completed 8 weeks of treatment
delivery.note: Seven subjects (2, 2 and 3) had no follow-up diary, leaving 190 in the analysis.

delivery.label: Analysis population
delivery.value: Intention to treat, with the most recent bladder diary used for subjects who did not finish treatment; 190 of 197 analyzed

reports.label: Combined therapy extension
reports.dateLocator: PubMed: J Am Geriatr Soc April 2000;48(4)
reports.citation: Burgio KL, Locher JL, Goode PS. "Combined Behavioral and Drug Therapy for Urge Incontinence in Older Women." *J Am Geriatr Soc.* 2000;48(4):370-374. doi:10.1111/j.1532-5415.2000.tb04692.x
reports.followUp: Second 8-week phase of combined therapy after 8 weeks of a single treatment

results.measure: Mean percent reduction after adding oxybutynin to behavioral training, in the 8 subjects (12.7%) not dry or satisfied after behavioral training alone: single therapy versus combined
results.note: Modified crossover extension; only subjects not totally continent or not satisfied were offered combined therapy, so there is no concurrent control.

results.measure: Mean percent reduction after adding behavioral training to oxybutynin, in the 27 subjects (41.5%) not dry or satisfied after drug alone: single therapy versus combined
results.note: 35 subjects in all entered combined treatment.

reports.label: Urodynamic analysis
reports.dateLocator: PubMed: J Am Geriatr Soc May 2002;50(5)
reports.citation: Goode PS, Burgio KL, Locher JL, Umlauf MG, Lloyd LK, Roth DL. "Urodynamic Changes Associated with Behavioral and Drug Treatment of Urge Incontinence in Older Women." *J Am Geriatr Soc.* 2002;50(5):808-816. doi:10.1046/j.1532-5415.2002.50204.x
reports.followUp: 8 weeks of treatment; 105 women with cystometry before and after treatment

results.measure: Mean change in cystometric capacity, mL (n = 105)
results.note: The parent report gives +70.9 mL and -5.9 mL for oxybutynin and placebo in the same subsample.

results.measure: Mean increase in volume at strong desire to void, mL
Detrusor instability resolved after treatment, among women who had it at baseline
Mean percent reduction in incontinent episodes in the urodynamic subsample (n = 105)
results.note: Structural equation modeling did not show that the improvement was mediated by the urodynamic or voiding-frequency changes.

reports.label: Nocturia analysis
reports.dateLocator: PubMed: J Am Geriatr Soc May 2005;53(5)
reports.citation: Johnson TM 2nd, Burgio KL, Redden DT, Wright KC, Goode PS. "Effects of Behavioral and Drug Therapy on Nocturia in Older Incontinent Women." *J Am Geriatr Soc.* 2005;53(5):846-850. doi:10.1111/j.1532-5415.2005.53260.x
reports.followUp: 8 weeks of treatment; 131 of 197 women had nocturia at baseline

results.measure: Median reduction in nocturia episodes per night (secondary analysis of the parent trial)
results.note: Behavioral versus placebo P < .001; oxybutynin versus placebo P = .007.

relations.note: Both compared a nondrug overactive bladder treatment with an antimuscarinic; ORBIT used tibial nerve stimulation against tolterodine.
